issues.why: Codebase name from checkout dir (main.rs:393,419-424) makes ids/bytes differ across clones.
Stack overflow aborts the process, isolate.rs.
Seal does not record extraction options; --tests mismatch makes symbols Absent (main.rs:73-74).
Non-UTF-8 file skipped silently at source.rs:181.
Trait map truncates to first max_edges with no omitted count, overview.rs:236.
Untyped closure params name-matched to internal methods (extract.rs:351).
Finding mentions resolution against an outer same-named variable's type but gives it little emphasis.
verify fails on own repo because MER-02 example id is read as citation, check.rs:390.
ignore 0.4.30 breaks MSRV 1.85 without the lock pin.
Same ignore 0.4.30 needs newer Rust than declared.
Closure bound by let is drawn at definition, later calls dropped.
Re-entry depth limit of 8 at resolve.rs:642 turns paths into External ids.

findings.why: Topic then lock written non-atomically, but verify deliberately flags the orphan pointer and re-running sign repairs it; 'permanent' and manual git recovery are overstated.
Deletion keys on a front-matter marker alone, as designed; only .md files with sealmap: as first key are affected, which is an unlikely collision.
parse_canonical compares to_toml() byte-for-byte and does not normalise \r\n, so a CRLF checkout fails verify as NonCanonical; the code documents this.
Matches seal not recording extraction options.
Matches the trait map truncation without omitted count.
Matches false guesses from untyped closure parameters.
Matches verify failing on its own repository.
Matches the MSRV vs ignore dependency issue.
Matches the let-bound closure drawn at its definition.
Each method's sig fingerprint feeds impl_header (attrs, generics, trait, self type, where), so an impl-header edit changes every method's sig_hash.
The corpus statement 'none of the 0.2 crates is published' does contradict the README/DESIGN 'published as 0.2.0' (a doc drift), but the claimed seal reproducibility consequence is speculative.
